question: In thyroid eye disease, dysthyroid optic neuropathy (DON) is most commonly caused by direct optic nerve compression at the orbital apex by enlarged extraocular muscles rather than by vascular ischaemia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Apical muscle crowding — not vascular ischaemia — is the dominant mechanism of optic nerve damage in DON. CT or MRI shows enlarged extraocular muscles (typically medial and inferior recti) converging at the apex and impinging on the optic nerve. The absence of proptosis does NOT exclude DON; a tight orbit can cause DON with minimal exophthalmos.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. DON occurs when hypertrophied extraocular muscles (particularly medial and inferior recti) compress the optic nerve at the apex of the orbit — the site of maximal anatomical constraint. This 'crowded orbital apex' reduces visual acuity, colour vision, and produces a relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD). Urgent high-dose IV methylprednisolone ± orbital decompression is required to prevent permanent visual loss.
